newsitem.title: CHILE: Canada trade pact still stalled in Chilean Congress.
newsitem.headline: Canada trade pact still stalled in Chilean Congress.

text.p: A free trade agreement between Chile and Canada officially went into effect in Canada on Tuesday but not in Chile because the country's Senate has yet to ratify the agreement, Foreign Minister Jose Miguel Insulza.

With the treaty in limbo as it awaits final congressional approval, expected on Wednesday, Insulza said his government was not overly concerned if the vote were delayed a day or two -- but no longer than that.

The trade pact, signed by the leaders of both governments last year, cannot take effect until it is ratified by the Chilean Senate. Since Canadian lawmakers have already approved it, the treaty formally went into effect as scheduled in Canada on Tuesday, but not in Chile.

"I hope they (in Congress) resolve this issue soon. There's a problem with when the treaty will take effect, but it's nothing serious if it's only a day or two," Insulza told Chilean reporters by telephone from Singapore.

The Chilean Senate was scheduled to vote on the trade agreement on Wednesday. It is expected to pass but opponents, mostly rightist lawmakers from agricultural districts, have been stalling the vote and trying to win concessions from President Eduardo Frei's government on other trade issues.
Insulza said the two countries may have to find some way of accounting for the fact that the treaty, assuming it passes, took effect in Canada two days before it did in Chile.
"We will have to find an ad hoc mechanism to resolve the problem of those two days when the treaty was in effect in Canada and not in Chile," he said.

If it passes, the treaty will sweep away tariffs on about 80 percent of trade between the two countries. The rest, including on many sensitive farm products, will be phased out over the next 18 years.

Opponents of the treaty sent the treaty "for study" to the Senate's Environment Committee, but party leaders instructed the committee to give an oral report on Wednesday on its conclusions about the treaty, followed by a full Senate vote.
